  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our Distribution revenue&#160;accounted for 36.0%&#160;of our total revenue in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 and 37.7%&#160;of our total revenue in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. During the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, Distribution segment revenue&#160;was&#160;$30.2&#160;million which was an&#160;increase of $5.0 million or 19.8%.&#160; This increase was primarily due to&#160;incremental traditional rental revenue and&#160;higher&#160;revenue from&#160;our non-rental products.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Distribution segment revenue&#160;increase for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 versus the third quarter of fiscal year 2025&#160;was primarily due to a favorable sales mix driven by rental revenue.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Distribution revenue&#160;includes orders for instruments that we routinely stock in our inventory, customized products, and other products ordered less frequently, which we do not stock. Product backorders are the total dollar value of orders received for which revenue has not yet been recognized. Pending product shipments are primarily backorders, but also include products that are requested to be calibrated in our service centers prior to shipment, orders required by the customer to be shipped complete or at a future date, and other orders awaiting final credit or management review prior to shipment. Management uses pending product shipments and backorders as measures of our future business performance and financial performance within the distribution segment.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total gross profit for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 was $25.3&#160;million, an increase of $5.6&#160;million or 28.3%&#160;versus the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. Total gross margin was 30.1%&#160;in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, up&#160;from 29.5%&#160;in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025, a 0.6% increase.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Service gross profit in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased $3.1&#160;million, or 25.2%, from the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. Service gross margin was&#160;28.8%&#160;in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, a&#160;decrease of 0.9% compared to 29.7%&#160;in the&#160;third quarter of fiscal year 2025. This decrease in Service&#160;gross margin was the result of lower margin on traditional calibration services&#160;as we onboard new customers and&#160;an increase in outsourced&#160;services'&#160;costs, which was partially offset by strong margins on&#160;calibration services provided by recent acquisitions.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our Distribution gross margin includes net sales less the direct cost of inventory sold and the direct costs of equipment rental revenues, primarily depreciation expense for the fixed assets in our rental equipment pool, as well as the impact of rebates&#160;we receive from vendors, freight billed to customers, freight expenses and direct shipping costs. In general, our Distribution gross margin can vary based upon the mix of products sold.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total operating expenses were $25.2&#160;million in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 versus $17.6&#160;million during the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. The year-over-year increase in selling, marketing and warehouse expenses is primarily due to increased expenses related to recent acquisitions, including acquisition-related amortization&#160;expense and payroll costs. &#160;The increase in general and administrative expenses is primarily due to an increase in stock-based compensation, executive transition costs&#160;and increased payroll costs for new and acquired employees.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">As a percentage of total revenue, operating expenses were 30.0%&#160;in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 and 26.3%&#160;in the&#160;third quarter of fiscal year 2025, an increase of 3.7%.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Net income for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;decreased $3.5&#160;million or 146.7% versus&#160;the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. As a percentage of revenue, net loss the third&#160;quarter of fiscal year 2026 was (1.3%), and net income in the third&#160;quarter of fiscal year 2025 was 3.5%. The year-over-year decrease in net income was primarily due to lower operating income and&#160;higher&#160;interest expense, net. The increase in interest expense is related to the borrowing for the acquisition of Essco as well as an increase in interest rates on the Company's Credit Agreement.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Adjusted EBITDA:</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 was $10.1&#160;million, an increase of $2.2&#160;million or 27.2%&#160;versus the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. See &#8220;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#8221; below for a description of the non-GAAP measures we use and a reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measures. As a percentage of revenue, Adjusted EBITDA increased to 12.0%&#160;for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 from 11.9%&#160;for the third quarter of fiscal year 2025. The increase in Adjusted EBITDA during the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 was primarily driven by depreciation and amortization expense, non-cash stock compensation,&#160;interest expense and executive transition costs.</p>

This year-over-year increase included $25.1 million in service revenue from the acquisitions of Martin and Essco.</p>

This year-over-year increase included $3.4 million in revenue from the acquisitions of Martin and Essco and revenue increases across all distribution channels.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total gross profit for the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026 was $77.8&#160;million, an increase of $14.3&#160;million or 22.5%&#160;versus the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. Total gross margin was 32.1%&#160;in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026, slightly up from 31.6%&#160;in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025, a 0.5% increase.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Service gross profit in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased $6.8 million, or 16.4%, from the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. Service gross margin was 31.3%&#160;in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026, a 1.0% decrease versus&#160;32.3%&#160;in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. This small decrease in Service&#160;gross margin was the result of lower margins on traditional calibration services.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Distribution gross profit in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026&#160;increased $7.5&#160;million, or 34.3%, from the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. Distribution gross margin was&#160;33.6%&#160;in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026, a 3.4% increase versus&#160;30.2%&#160;in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025.&#160;Distribution gross margin improvement is primarily due to a favorable sales mix driven by rental revenue.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total operating expenses were $68.9 million in the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026 versus $52.6 million during the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. The increase in general and administrative expenses is primarily due to&#160;an increase in stock-based compensation, executive transition costs and an increase&#160;in payroll-related costs.</p>

Our provision for income taxes is affected by discrete items that may occur in any given period but are not consistent from year to year. The discrete benefits related to share-based compensation activity in&#160;the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal years 2026 and&#160;2025 was an expense of less than $0.1&#160;million and a benefit of $1.3&#160;million, respectively.&#160;We continue to evaluate our tax provision on a quarterly basis and adjust, as deemed necessary, our effective tax rate given changes in facts and circumstances expected in the future.</p>

     <td style="width: 9%; text-align: right; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt;">(65.9</td>
     <td style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt;">)%</td>
    </tr>

   </tbody>
  </table>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Net income for the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026&#160;decreased $6.6&#160;million or 65.9% versus&#160;the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025.&#160;&#160;As a percentage of revenue, net income was 1.4%&#160;in the first nine months of fiscal year 2026, down&#160;from 5.0%&#160;in the first nine months of fiscal year 2025.&#160;&#160;The year-over-year decrease in net income was primarily due to&#160;higher&#160;interest expense, net, and higher depreciation and amortization expenses.&#160;The increase in interest expense is related to the borrowing for the acquisition of Essco as well as an increase in interest rates on the Company's Credit Agreement. Increased depreciation and amortization expense is primarily due to the Company's recent acquisitions.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Adjusted EBITDA:</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Total Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, for the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026 was $34.0&#160;million, an increase of $7.0&#160;million or 25.8%&#160;versus the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. See &#8220;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#8221; below for a description of the non-GAAP measures we use and a reconciliation to the most directly comparable GAAP measures. As a percentage of revenue, Adjusted EBITDA increased to 14.0%&#160;for the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026 from 13.4%&#160;for the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2025. The increase in Adjusted EBITDA during the&#160;first&#160;nine months of fiscal year 2026 was primarily driven by depreciation and amortization expense, non-cash stock compensation,&#160;interest expense and income tax expense.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Non-GAAP Financial Measures</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Service Organic Revenue Growth</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">In addition to reporting service revenue growth, a GAAP measure, we present service organic revenue growth (current period service revenue less freight billed to customer less acquired revenue less prior period service revenue/prior period service revenue less freight billed to customer less divested&#160;revenue times 100). Acquired revenue is revenue generated from acquisitions for&#160;twelve&#160;months subsequent to the acquisition date. Divested revenue is revenue in the prior period related to businesses that were divested in the last twelve months. The Company's management believes service organic revenue growth is an important measure of operating performance because the measure provides a basis for comparison of our business operations across periods to assess core operating performance. As such, the Company uses service organic revenue growth as a measure of performance when evaluating its Service segment and as a basis for planning and forecasting.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Service organic growth is not a measure of financial performance under GAAP and is not calculated through the application of GAAP. As such, it should not be considered as a substitute or alternative for the GAAP measure of net income and, therefore, should not be used in isolation of, but in conjunction with, the GAAP measure. Service organic growth, as presented, may produce results that vary from the GAAP measure and may not be comparable to a similarly defined non-GAAP measure used by other companies.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Adjusted EBITDA</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">In addition to reporting net income, a GAAP measure, we present Adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, executive transition costs, non-cash stock compensation expense, gain on sale of assets, acquisition-related transaction expenses, contingent consideration, and certain other expenses), which is a non-GAAP measure. Our management believes Adjusted EBITDA is an important measure of our operating performance because it allows management, investors and others to evaluate and compare the performance of our core operations from period to period by removing the impact of the capital structure (interest), tangible and intangible asset base (depreciation and amortization), taxes, stock-based compensation expense, executive transition costs&#160;and other items, which is not always commensurate with the reporting period in which it is included. As such, our management uses Adjusted EBITDA as a measure of performance when evaluating our business segments and as a basis for planning and forecasting. Adjusted EBITDA is also commonly used by rating agencies, lenders and other parties to evaluate our credit worthiness.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">Adjusted EBITDA is not a measure of financial performance under GAAP and is not calculated through the application of GAAP. As such, it should not be considered as a substitute or alternative for the GAAP measure of net income and, therefore, should not be used in isolation of, but in conjunction with, the GAAP measure. Adjusted EBITDA, as presented, may produce results that vary from the GAAP measure and may not be comparable to a similarly defined non-GAAP measure used by other companies.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">In addition to reporting Diluted Earnings Per Share, a GAAP measure, we present Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share (net income plus acquisition-related amortization expense, acquisition-related transaction expenses, executive transition costs, acquisition-related stock-based compensation&#160;and acquisition amortization of backlog; divided by the average diluted shares outstanding during the period), which is a non-GAAP measure. Our management believes Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share is an important measure of our operating performance because it provides a basis for comparison of our business operations between current, past and future periods by excluding items that we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share is not a measure of financial performance under GAAP and is not calculated through the application of GAAP. As such, it should not be considered as a substitute or alternative for the GAAP measure of Diluted Earnings Per Share and, therefore, should not be used in isolation of, but in conjunction with, the GAAP measure. Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share, as presented, may produce results that vary from the GAAP measure and may not be comparable to a similarly defined non-GAAP measure used by other companies.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">We expect that foreseeable liquidity and capital resource requirements will be met through cash and cash equivalents, anticipated cash flows from operations and borrowings from our revolving credit facility. We believe that these sources of financing will be adequate to meet our future requirements including anticipated operating expenses, capital expenditures, interest payments on our long-term debt, and planned business acquisitions. To the extent that we&#160;do&#160;not satisfy our&#160;liquidity requirements through cash and cash equivalents, anticipated cash flows from operations and borrowings from our revolving credit facility, we&#160;intend&#160;to satisfy such requirements through proceeds from the issuance of common stock.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt;">On July 29, 2025, we entered into a Credit Agreement (the &#8220;Credit Agreement&#8221;) with a group of three lenders establishing a new five-year $150.0 million secured revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Credit Facility&#8221;). Borrowing options under the Credit Facility include: (i) a revolving loan option; (ii) a swingline loan option; and (iii) letters of credit, each of which is provided on a committed basis. The Credit Facility replaced the Company&#8217;s former $80.0 million credit facility (the &#8220;Replaced Facility&#8221;), which included a letter of credit subfacility of $10.0 million and our 2018 term loan, with an original principal amount of $15.0 million (the &#8220;2018 Term Loan&#8221;). We used initial borrowings under the Credit Facility to repay amounts due under the Replaced Facility, including the remaining amounts under the 2018 Term Loan, and for the acquisition of Essco.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Under the Credit Agreement, we can&#160;use up to $50.0 million for acquisitions in any single fiscal year, with an exception for the Essco acquisition. In addition, we are permitted to make restricted payments up to $25.0 million in the aggregate over the term of the Credit Facility and up to $10.0 million in any single fiscal year to repurchase shares and pay dividends.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">As of December 27, 2025, $150.0 million&#160;was available for borrowing, subject to covenant restrictions,&#160;under the Credit Facility, of which, $99.9 million was outstanding. &#160;During the&#160;first nine months of fiscal year 2026, we used approximately $83.0<b>&#160;</b>million,&#160;drawn from the Credit Facility, for a business acquisition.&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">Most borrowings under the Credit Facility bear interest, at our election, at a fixed base rate or the daily simple SOFR rate, plus a margin. Any swingline loan will bear interest at the fixed base rate plus a margin. The applicable margin is based on our then-current leverage ratio. Under the Credit Facility, the applicable margin was reduced for most levels of leverage ratio for comparable categories of borrowings under the Replaced Facility. The applicable margin ranges from 0.00% to 0.75% for base rate loans and 1.00% to 1.75% for SOFR loans. We will pay a commitment fee based on the daily unused amount under the Credit Facility multiplied by the applicable margin, which ranges from 0.10% to 0.20%.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">The Credit Agreement has certain financial covenants with which we must comply. The leverage ratio covenant under the Credit Agreement requires us to maintain our ratio of outstanding indebtedness to consolidated EBITDA to be no greater than 3.00 to 1.00, provided that we may temporarily increase the leverage ratio covenant if we complete a material permitted acquisition under the terms of the Credit Agreement. The Company's leverage ratio, as defined in the Credit Agreement, was 2.00&#160;on December 27, 2025, compared with 0.78 on March 29, 2025. We must also maintain a fixed charge coverage ratio of no less than 1.20 to 1.00.&#160;We were in compliance with all loan covenants and requirements of the Credit Agreement and the Replaced Facility, as applicable, during the&#160;first nine&#160;months of fiscal year 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

     <td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Inventory: Our inventory strategy includes making appropriate large quantity, high dollar purchases with key manufacturers for various reasons, including maximizing on-hand availability of key products, expanding the number of SKUs stocked in anticipation of customer demand, reducing backorders for products with long lead times and optimizing vendor purchase and sales volume discounts. As a result, inventory levels may vary from quarter-to-quarter based on the timing of these large orders in relation to our quarter end. Any&#160;decreases in inventory are primarily due to the timing of shipments relative to strategic inventory purchases during the periods.</p> </td>

In addition, we used $1.8&#160;million for&#160;repayments of our term loan.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b>Operating Free Cash Flow</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">In addition to reporting net cash from operations,&#160;a GAAP&#160;measure, we present Operating Free Cash Flow (net cash from operations less capital expenditures), which is a non-GAAP measure. The Company&#8217;s management believes Operating Free Cash Flow is an important liquidity measure that reflects the cash generated by the business, after the purchases of technology, capabilities and assets, that can then be used for, among other things, strategic acquisitions, investments in the business and funding ongoing operations.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Operating Free Cash Flow is not a measure of financial performance under GAAP and is not calculated through the application of GAAP. As such, it should not be considered as a substitute or alternative for the GAAP measure of net cash from operations and, therefore, should not be used in isolation of, but in conjunction with, the GAAP measure. Operating Free Cash Flow, as presented, may produce results that vary from the GAAP measure and may not be comparable to a similarly defined non-GAAP measure used by other companies.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>OUTLOOK</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our&#160;team delivered a strong quarter of revenue and adjusted EBITDA (a non-GAAP measure) performance in the fiscal third quarter highlighted by double-digit service revenue and gross profit growth. Service organic revenue growth was 7%, Distribution revenue grew 19.8% in the quarter with a gross margin of&#160;32.4%, driven primarily by the strategic mix increase of higher-margin rentals. While the Company's net income decreased by more than 100% over the prior year period, the team's execution and robust revenue growth enabled us to deliver 27% adjusted EBITDA (a non-GAAP measure) growth.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We believe we are well-positioned to execute our acquisition strategy while returning to more historic levels of service organic growth.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Looking forward, we are optimistic given the momentum building in our service segment driven by strong retention, increased customer activity levels, and realization of business wins. We expect high single-digit Service organic revenue growth for the balance of fiscal 2026, barring any increased economic uncertainty. We believe our strong value proposition along with&#160;the recent acquisitions of premier service calibration&#160;companies that expand our&#160;geographical footprint&#160;positions us well to drive sustainable, long-term shareholder value.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">We expect our&#160;income tax rate to range between 30% and 32% for full fiscal year 2026. This estimate includes federal, various state, Canadian and Irish income taxes and reflects the discrete tax accounting associated with share-based payment awards.</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="qqdmr" title="qqdmr" href="#"></a>ITEM 3. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>INTEREST RATES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Our exposure to changes in interest rates results from our borrowing activities.&#160; In the event interest rates were to move by 1%, our yearly interest expense would increase or decrease by approximately $1.0&#160;million assuming our borrowing levels at December 27, 2025&#160;remained constant under the Credit Facility.&#160;As of December 27, 2025, $150.0&#160;million&#160;was available for borrowing,&#160;under the Credit Facility, of which $99.9&#160;million was outstanding.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Under the Credit Agreement, effective as of July 29, 2025, at our option, we are permitted to borrow from the Credit Facility at a base rate or&#160;the variable&#160;Daily Simple SOFR&#160;(subject to a 1.00% floor), in each case, plus a margin. Our interest rate margin is determined on a quarterly basis based upon our calculated leverage ratio. Our weighted average interest rate for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026&#160;for the Credit Facility&#160;was 5.7%. On December 27, 2025, we had no hedging arrangements in place for our Credit Facility&#160;to limit our exposure to movements in interest rates.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>FOREIGN CURRENCY</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Approximately 93%&#160;and 92% of our total revenues for the first nine months of fiscal year 2026 and 2025, respectively were denominated in U.S. dollars, with the remainder denominated in Canadian dollars and Euros. A 10% change in the value of the Canadian dollar to the U.S. dollar and the Euro to the U.S. dollar would impact our revenue by less than 1%. We monitor the relationship between the U.S. dollar and the Canadian dollar and the U.S. dollar and the Euro on a monthly basis and adjust sales prices for products and services sold in Canadian dollars or Euros as we believe to be appropriate.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">We&#160;utilized short-term foreign exchange forward contracts to reduce the risk that future earnings denominated in Canadian dollars would be adversely affected by changes in currency exchange rates. We did&#160;not apply hedge accounting and therefore the net change in the fair value of the contracts, which totaled a<b>&#160;</b>loss&#160;of less than $0.1&#160;million and a gain of $0.2&#160;million<b>&#160;</b>in&#160;the first nine months of&#160;fiscal years 2026 and 2025, respectively, was recognized as a component of Interest and Other (Income) Expense, net in the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="cps" title="cps" href="#"></a>ITEM 4. CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Conclusion Regarding the Effectiveness of Disclosure Controls and Procedures.</b> Our principal executive officer and our principal financial officer evaluated our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;), Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) as of the end of the period covered by this quarterly report. Disclosure controls and procedures are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in our reports filed under the Exchange Act&#160;is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our principal executive officer and principal financial officer to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. Based on this evaluation, our principal executive officer and our principal financial officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of such date.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting.</b> The Company's internal controls over financial reporting included those inherited from the Martin acquisition, which have been evaluated by management and supplemented where deemed appropriate. Our management, with the participation of our principal executive officer and principal&#160;financial officer, did not identify any other changes that occurred in our internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended December 27, 2025, that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
